To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Policy mixes for energy transitions are more effective if they are consistent, coherent and credible and if the policy processes are inclusive.”

(i) a broader perspective on policy mixes for sustainability is needed that (ii) explicitly considers overarching policy mix characteristics, policy strategies, policy design and policy process aspects, (iii) which are crucial to understand the effectiveness of policy mixes in terms of their contribution to sustainability, (iv) and that this requires a more comprehensive analysis of the interactions between instruments and the involved actors, institutions and processes.
Policy mixes can foster energy transitions by addressing barriers to change, such as lock-in and path dependencies, through a multiplicity of complementary instruments.

the following questions: How do policy mixes evolve?
the design of policy instruments for the energy transition, the analysis of the interplay of instruments and policy processes and the analysis of overarching characteristics of policy mixes.
